question: Compare the photon energies corresponding to the transitions $n=3$ to $n=2$ and $n=4$ to $n=2$ in hydrogen atom. Which transition emits a photon of greater energy? Justify your answer.

options.A: $\Delta E_{3\to2}=1.89\text{ eV}$ and $\Delta E_{4\to2}=1.51\text{ eV}$; hence $3\to2$ emits greater energy.
options.B: Both transitions emit equal photon energy because they end at $n=2$.
options.C: $\Delta E_{3\to2}=2.55\text{ eV}$ and $\Delta E_{4\to2}=1.89\text{ eV}$; hence $3\to2$ emits greater energy.
options.D: $E_3=-1.51\text{ eV}$, $E_4=-0.85\text{ eV}$ and $E_2=-3.40\text{ eV}$. Thus $\Delta E_{3\to2}=1.89\text{ eV}$ and $\Delta E_{4\to2}=2.55\text{ eV}$. Therefore $4\to2$ emits the greater-energy photon.
